title: Flip Columns for Maximum Equal Rows
description:
You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `matrix` containing only `0`s and `1`s.

You may choose any number of columns (including zero) and flip every cell in those chosen columns (changing `0` to `1` and `1` to `0`).

Return the **maximum number of rows** that have all values equal (either all `0`s or all `1`s) after applying an optimal subset of column flips.
hints: Two rows can simultaneously become all-equal after the same subset of column flips if and only if they are identical or exact bitwise complements of each other.
Canonicalize every row by flipping all its bits whenever row[0] == 1, then count the frequency of each canonical pattern with a hash map.

examples.explanation: No matter which columns are flipped, at most 1 row can have all equal values (rows [0,1] and [1,1] are neither equal nor complements).
Flipping column 0 turns [0,1] into [1,1] and [1,0] into [0,0], giving 2 all-equal rows.
Flipping column 0 makes rows 1 and 2 all-equal ([1,1,1] and [0,0,0]), giving 2 rows.
